thread.title: Apple Cash Repatriation Could Spur Acquisitions, Investor Returns

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: Apple Cash Repatriation Could Spur Acquisitions, Investor Returns
text:
Apple ( AAPL ) shares climbed to a record high on Thursday on news the iPhone maker plans to bring most of its foreign cash stockpile to the U.S. to fund domestic expansion efforts and possibly increased acquisitions and returns to shareholders.
Apple shares inched up 0.1% to close at 179.26   In intraday trading, it notched an all-time high of 180.05.
Apple is expected to bring home $245 billion in foreign profits banked overseas to pay for capital expenditures (including a new campus and more data centers), fund U.S. manufacturing deals and create 20,000 new jobs over the next five years. Apple had about $252 billion in overseas cash and marketable securities as of Sept. 30.
Apple anticipates a U.S. tax bill of about $38 billion to bring the foreign cash to the U.S., based on the temporary tax rate of 15.5% on foreign profits. On Wednesday Apple said it plans to contribute more than $350 billion to the U.S. economy over the next five years.
In addition to funding expanded domestic operations, Apple could use the cash windfall for a "higher frequency of small technology acquisitions and more aggressive return of cash to shareholders," Piper Jaffray analyst Michael Olson said in a note to clients.
It is doubtful that Apple will use the cash to make a large acquisition, such as for Netflix ( NFLX ) or Tesla ( TSLA ), as some analysts have fantasized.
"It would be out of character for Apple to do a large acquisition with the repatriated cash (as has been widely discussed in the media), but we would not be surprised to see an increase in the company's appetite for gobbling up smaller strategic technology businesses," Olson said. "Additionally, the transfer of a significant portion of the company's cash balance to the U.S. could result in more aggressive return of cash to shareholders."
Return of cash to shareholders could take the form of stock buybacks or increased dividends.
